verses.verse:
आहतोऽनाहतश्चैव तथाऽतीतश्च कथ्यते।
अविरामी विरामीति त्रिघायी बहुधा भवेत्।१४३।
verses.text: The tihāī is said to be āhat, anāhat and atīt, and without pauses or with pauses; thus it is of many kinds.

commentary.text: That is, with the last syllable of some tihāīs the sam note is struck at once (on the first mātrā); and the last syllable of some tihāīs falls ahead of or behind the sam - these are called atīt (landing after sam) and anāghāt (landing off sam). Some tihāīs have more pause, some little pause, and in some there is no pause at all. In this way there are many tihāīs. Tihāīs that take more than one āvartan are called cakkardār tihāīs. If tihāīs are shorter than one āvartan, they are used in the second half of the tāla, so that the duty of reaching the sam can be fulfilled. Now, if you try to make tihāīs from three mātrās up to 16 mātrās in the form of notes, words and tāla bols, attend to the following points.
